reason: Rank the guarded B prefetch first: it is a small change to the active K loop, and its 2,048-byte lookahead matches the supplied B stride and 128-byte cache-line evidence. The hint and guard still add timed work, so benefit is unverified. The two B-panel proposals describe the same packed layout; keep them adjacent and treat either result as evidence about that layout, not as independent confirmation. The active loop already uses four ZA tiles, so changing FMOPA order or moving loop control has limited expected benefit. A-stride padding lacks cache-set evidence and increases scratch use. A transpose fusion repeats A reads across 16 column panels; the separate A-transpose proposal applies to fallback sizes, outside the fixed n=512 timing.
